outcomes: Inspect a Dataset sample and a DataLoader batch as explicit image-and-target contracts.
Build reproducible bird-versus-airplane subsets without allowing validation data to affect training transforms or statistics.
Train a classifier from raw logits with CrossEntropyLoss and a correct optimizer loop.
Evaluate class behavior separately under eval() and inference_mode(), then save the best state.

sections.title: Let Dataset define one sample
sections.summary: A map-style Dataset maps an index to a sample and normally reports its length.
body: TorchVision's CIFAR10 dataset returns an image and an integer class target. Before constructing a model, inspect several examples, class names, shape, dtype, and range. A Dataset contract describes one item; batching belongs to DataLoader.
A custom map-style Dataset implements __getitem__ and usually __len__. Keeping data access outside the training loop makes it possible to test labels and preprocessing without invoking a model.

code.title: Inspect CIFAR-10 before batching
code.source:
from torchvision import datasets

raw_train = datasets.CIFAR10(root="data", train=True, download=True)
image, target = raw_train[0]
print(type(image), image.size, target, raw_train.classes[target])
assert 0 <= target < len(raw_train.classes)

points: A sample target is an integer class index.
A transform belongs to the sample path and runs when the item is fetched.
Training and validation datasets may reference the same source format but need different transforms.
Visual inspection can reveal label, channel, and scaling mistakes early.

sections.title: Build separate training and validation transforms
sections.summary: Training augmentation adds plausible variation; validation preprocessing remains deterministic.
body: TorchVision transforms v2 provides the current image transformation path. Convert the image representation explicitly, scale integer values while converting to float, then normalize with a declared baseline or statistics estimated from training data only. The current official CIFAR-10 tutorial uses 0.5 for each channel's mean and standard deviation as a simple fixed baseline.

Random crop or horizontal flip may improve the training distribution, but repeating random augmentation during validation makes metrics noisy and changes what is being evaluated. Share only deterministic preparation between the paths.

code.title: Two transform contracts
code.source:
import torch
from torchvision.transforms import v2

# Fixed baseline used by the current official CIFAR-10 tutorial.
normalize = v2.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
train_transform = v2.Compose([
    v2.ToImage(),
    v2.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
    v2.ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True),
    normalize,
])
validation_transform = v2.Compose([
    v2.ToImage(),
    v2.ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True),
    normalize,
])

callouts.title: Statistics can leak
callouts.body: When statistics are estimated for a new dataset, fit them on training samples only and reuse them unchanged for validation and test data.

sections.title: Map ten classes to two without losing provenance
sections.summary: Filtering and target remapping should remain inspectable and identical across splits.
body: CIFAR-10 labels airplanes as 0 and birds as 2. The binary task needs both a subset of indices and a target map to contiguous class indices 0 and 1. Keep the original-to-new mapping beside the class names so predictions remain interpretable.

Partition source indices before any item is fetched or augmented. Then attach the training and deterministic validation transforms to separate dataset views over the same source samples, apply the same target mapping, and reserve the official test split for one final evaluation.

sections.title: Use DataLoader to batch and schedule access
sections.summary: DataLoader adds sampling order, collation, multiprocessing, and optional pinned memory around a Dataset.
body: Training commonly shuffles indices each epoch, while validation uses a stable order. The default collator stacks compatible tensors and prepends the batch axis, turning image samples C × H × W into N × C × H × W.

Start with num_workers=0 for readable errors, then measure larger values on the actual system. pin_memory and persistent_workers are performance options rather than correctness requirements. Windows multiprocessing code must keep executable setup behind the documented main guard.

For a reproducible model-selection split, partition the original training indices with a seeded generator before transforms run. Use a second view of the training files for deterministic validation preprocessing, and keep the dataset's official test split outside the tuning loop.

code.title: Build a leak-free binary pipeline
code.source:
import torch
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Dataset
from torchvision import datasets
from torchvision.transforms import v2

class BinaryCIFAR(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, base, mapping, indices=None):
        self.base = base
        self.mapping = dict(mapping)
        candidates = range(len(base)) if indices is None else indices
        self.indices = [i for i in candidates if base.targets[i] in self.mapping]

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.indices)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        image, original_target = self.base[self.indices[index]]
        return image, self.mapping[original_target]

label_map = {0: 0, 2: 1}  # airplane, bird
normalize = v2.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
train_transform = v2.Compose([
    v2.ToImage(),
    v2.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
    v2.ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True),
    normalize,
])
validation_transform = v2.Compose([
    v2.ToImage(),
    v2.ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True),
    normalize,
])

# Download once, then split selected training indices before transforms run.
raw_train = datasets.CIFAR10(root="data", train=True, download=True)
split_generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(42)
train_indices, validation_indices = [], []
for original_label in label_map:
    class_indices = torch.tensor([
        i for i, target in enumerate(raw_train.targets) if target == original_label
    ])
    order = torch.randperm(len(class_indices), generator=split_generator)
    class_indices = class_indices[order]
    validation_count = len(class_indices) // 10
    validation_indices.extend(class_indices[:validation_count].tolist())
    train_indices.extend(class_indices[validation_count:].tolist())

train_base = datasets.CIFAR10("data", train=True, transform=train_transform)
validation_base = datasets.CIFAR10("data", train=True, transform=validation_transform)
test_base = datasets.CIFAR10("data", train=False, transform=validation_transform)
train_data = BinaryCIFAR(train_base, label_map, train_indices)
validation_data = BinaryCIFAR(validation_base, label_map, validation_indices)
test_data = BinaryCIFAR(test_base, label_map)

loader_generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(43)
train_loader = DataLoader(
    train_data, batch_size=64, shuffle=True, num_workers=0, generator=loader_generator
)
validation_loader = DataLoader(validation_data, batch_size=128, shuffle=False, num_workers=0)
test_loader = DataLoader(test_data, batch_size=128, shuffle=False, num_workers=0)

images, targets = next(iter(train_loader))
assert images.shape[1:] == (3, 32, 32)
assert images.dtype == torch.float32
assert targets.dtype == torch.long
assert len(train_data) + len(validation_data) == 10_000
assert len(test_data) == 2_000

points: Shuffle training indices, not validation indices.
Use drop_last only when the model or metric truly requires equal batch sizes.
Tune workers after the data path is correct.
A custom collate function is required for variable-sized samples.

sections.title: Return logits and let the loss define the comparison
sections.summary: CrossEntropyLoss expects unnormalized class scores and integer or valid probability targets.
body: The historical notebook explores Softmax, LogSoftmax, NLLLoss, and CrossEntropyLoss. The modern default for a single-label classifier is simpler: the final layer returns one raw logit per class and CrossEntropyLoss performs the appropriate log-softmax comparison internally.
Adding Softmax or LogSoftmax before CrossEntropyLoss is redundant and changes the values the loss expects. Apply softmax to detached logits only when presenting probabilities.

code.title: A baseline two-class MLP
code.source:
import torch
from torch import nn

torch.manual_seed(42)
images = torch.randn(4, 3, 32, 32)
targets = torch.tensor([0, 1, 1, 0], dtype=torch.long)
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Flatten(),
    nn.Linear(3 * 32 * 32, 256),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(256, 2),
)
loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

logits = model(images)
loss = loss_fn(logits, targets)
assert logits.shape == (images.shape[0], 2)
assert loss.ndim == 0

callouts.title: No probability layer before cross entropy
callouts.body: CrossEntropyLoss expects logits that may be negative and do not need to sum to one.

sections.title: Keep training and validation paths visibly different
sections.summary: Training updates parameters; validation fixes them and measures behavior on unseen samples.
body: Move the model and each batch to the selected device at a clear boundary. During training, select train mode, clear gradients, compute logits and loss, backpropagate, and step. During validation, select eval mode and inference mode and do not touch the optimizer.

Overall accuracy can hide asymmetric mistakes. Accumulate a two-by-two confusion matrix so bird recall and airplane recall remain visible. Save a copy of the state dictionary when the chosen validation metric improves.

code.title: Train, select, and test without leakage
code.source:
import copy

import torch
from torch import nn

# Prerequisites: run "Build a leak-free binary pipeline" to define the three loaders,
# then run "A baseline two-class MLP" to define model and loss_fn.
accelerator = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator(check_available=True)
device = accelerator if accelerator is not None else torch.device("cpu")
model = model.to(device)
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=3e-4)

def train_one_epoch(model, loader, loss_fn, optimizer, device):
    model.train()
    total_loss, total_examples = 0.0, 0
    for images, targets in loader:
        images, targets = images.to(device), targets.to(device)
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss = loss_fn(model(images), targets)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        total_loss += loss.item() * targets.numel()
        total_examples += targets.numel()
    return total_loss / total_examples

def evaluate(model, loader, loss_fn, device):
    model.eval()
    total_loss, correct, total_examples = 0.0, 0, 0
    confusion = torch.zeros(2, 2, dtype=torch.int64)
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for images, targets in loader:
            images, targets = images.to(device), targets.to(device)
            logits = model(images)
            loss = loss_fn(logits, targets)
            predictions = logits.argmax(dim=1)
            total_loss += loss.item() * targets.numel()
            correct += (predictions == targets).sum().item()
            total_examples += targets.numel()
            flat = targets.cpu() * 2 + predictions.cpu()
            confusion += torch.bincount(flat, minlength=4).reshape(2, 2)
    return total_loss / total_examples, correct / total_examples, confusion

best_validation_loss = float("inf")
best_state = None
for epoch in range(2):
    training_loss = train_one_epoch(model, train_loader, loss_fn, optimizer, device)
    validation_loss, validation_accuracy, _ = evaluate(
        model, validation_loader, loss_fn, device
    )
    if validation_loss < best_validation_loss:
        best_validation_loss = validation_loss
        best_state = copy.deepcopy(model.state_dict())
    print(epoch, training_loss, validation_loss, validation_accuracy)

if best_state is None:
    raise RuntimeError("training did not produce a finite validation checkpoint")
model.load_state_dict(best_state)
torch.save(best_state, "best_binary_cifar.pt")
best_validation_loss, best_validation_accuracy, confusion = evaluate(
    model, validation_loader, loss_fn, device
)
recall = confusion.diag() / confusion.sum(dim=1).clamp_min(1)
print("best validation:", best_validation_loss, best_validation_accuracy)
print("validation confusion (truth rows, prediction columns):\n", confusion)
print("airplane recall, bird recall:", recall.tolist())

# The official test split is evaluated once, after model selection.
test_loss, test_accuracy, test_confusion = evaluate(model, test_loader, loss_fn, device)
print("test:", test_loss, test_accuracy, test_confusion.tolist())
